svg.aria-label: IQ-TREE3-GPU: an alignment of eight bacterial genomes becomes a tree; Felsenstein pruning computes conditional likelihoods up the tree; the same calculation runs on CPU and GPU, the GPU finishing first (5.31x measured for this example only; benchmark medians 1.33x at 20 threads and 6.97x at 1 thread); one NNI move reaches the maximum-likelihood tree.
svg.text: One column, site 2,270, is followed through every stage.
Children before parents, for 2,194 patterns x 4 rate categories. The vectors shown are recomputed here and match IQ-TREE to 1e-4.
The ratio above is measured for this example tree only. Across all benchmark datasets the median is 1.33× at 20 threads (n = 145)
and 6.97× at 1 thread (n = 30); speedup depends on the data. Same tree, same arithmetic, same log L on both sides.
IQ-TREE proposes the move; the GPU evaluates it. Both log L are real: LG+G4, branch lengths optimised on each topology.
UFBoot support, 1,000 replicates. The speedup of your own data depends on its size: see When it pays off below.
Example genome set shipped with the tool: examples/data/example_CAG-269.faa
8 gut genomes of the genus CAG-269, labelled by host. Every number in this animation is computed for this one alignment.
conditional likelihood of node v, from its children a, b
c runs over v's children; P(t) from LG, one per rate category
